title: Battle of music at Slaughter's Hall
summary: The Southern Serenaders stage a benefit battle of music so the stranded boys can go home.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I know that. And anyway, Charlie and Lem Johnson and all, were some little young cats like I had come up as a little youngster, because I'm older than Charlie, and you know, they're coming up, and they were the little cats of that time, so anyway, in order to get us out of Oklahoma City, the Southern Serenaders, at that time, said okay, said what we'll do is to play a battle of music up into Slaughter's Hall, and we'll give you all the proceeds so you can go home.
What town was that, you had the Slaughter's Hall in?
We have a Slaughter's Hall in Vicksburg, Mississippi, too.
I don't know why they called it Slaughter's Hall, maybe because they used to fight so much.
I think it was more from the stock yards.
They'd be in to kill the cows, and they called them the slaughterers, and this is their hall. I would prefer to think that way.
Well it might be. Then it could have been that the man that owned it, because it was a nice building --
His name could have been Slaughter.
Anyway, this -- these guys, we played a battle of music up there, and they gave us the proceeds, and we went back home.
